TLS handshake completion evidence
TLS negotiation completed and encrypted application data was observed.
Both hellos and subsequent encrypted application records were captured. Because the Finished messages are themselves encrypted, flowing application data is the strongest passive completion evidence.
Certificate trust and revocation boundary
Certificate trust and revocation were not evaluated.

No certificate was observable in this session (SEC-CERT-001 records why). Trust cannot be established from a packet capture: RFC 5280 SS6 defines path validation over a set of trust anchors, and a capture contains none. Revocation cannot be established either: OCSP and CRL retrieval are separate network transactions. Neither limitation is a finding against the certificate.
Implicit TLS session
The session used implicit TLS; no STARTTLS upgrade applies.

The connection was encrypted from its first record, so there is no cleartext upgrade dialogue to evaluate. The absence of a STARTTLS advertisement here is expected and is not a failure, a lack of support, or evidence of stripping.
Key exchange mechanism
Key exchange: ECDHE (x25519).
TLS 1.3 negotiates the key exchange in the ServerHello key_share extension; the cipher suite does not encode it (RFC 8446).
Forward secrecy
The negotiated key exchange provides forward secrecy.
RFC 8446 SS1.2 and App. D.5: TLS 1.3 removed static RSA and static Diffie-Hellman key exchange, so every TLS 1.3 suite is forward secret.
Certificate extraction
No certificate was observable in this session.

No certificate could be extracted because the negotiated TLS version encrypts the Certificate message, so it is structurally invisible to passive observation (RFC 8446 SS2). This is not a finding about the certificate itself: absence of certificate evidence is not evidence of an absent, invalid or untrusted certificate.
